evals.name: single-new-source

evals.expected_output: One new wiki page (or an update to the existing Redis Cache page) citing jira:INFRA-142, correct frontmatter, at least 2 outbound wikilinks, source-manifest/catalog/log updated, a lint-clean local git commit staged via propose-pr. Basic single-source sequence correctness.

evals.name: multi-source-one-session
evals.prompt: Three new sources about the rate-limiting middleware just landed under docs/sources/: ratelimit-design-doc.md (confluence:RATE-001, the design doc), ratelimit-implementation-ticket.md (jira:RATE-002, the implementation ticket), and ratelimit-slack-thread.md (slack:rate-limit-launch, the launch announcement). Ingest all three in one session.
evals.expected_output: One coherent ingest session covering all 3 sources — one source-scan, one build, one cross-linker pass, one lint, one propose-pr for the whole session (not one PR per source), each page citing the right source(s), at least 2 outbound wikilinks per page (stubs created if needed), log entries for each source. Tests the one-session/one-PR batching rule and multi-source citation.
files: fixture: run build_fixture.py <dest> from this directory, then point the agent at <dest>

evals.name: update-to-covered-source
evals.prompt: docs/sources/jira-auth-200.md (jira:AUTH-200) was just updated — the JWT token expiry changed from 24h to 1h. This source is already covered by the existing Auth Service wiki page. Make sure the wiki reflects the change.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes this as an update to an already-covered source (source-scan flags it 'needs --accept-covered'), confirms the change is real, re-scans with --accept-covered, and updates the Auth Service page's content (24h -> 1h) rather than creating a duplicate page or silently accepting the other two unrelated already-covered sources (INFRA-100, infra-overview-v1) that also show up as needing accept-covered but weren't actually asked about.
